deal.dialogue: You look well. Rich, even. So let's talk about the one thing you haven't spent. Sign, and the road gets easy.
A coin for your trouble. It's warm. It remembers where it was minted, and it will want to go home through your ribs.
That well gives you a sip of luck. I'm offering the whole bottle. The thing at the end of this road will laugh at that little blade. Let me give it teeth. Your skin will be thinner for it.
Wishing into a hole in the ground? Wish at me instead. I answer. A coin for your trouble. It's warm. It remembers where it was minted, and it will want to go home through your ribs.

That well gives you a sip of luck. I'm offering the whole bottle. A formality. Sign here and the road gets easy. Think of me as insurance. You'll never need the claim.
You're bleeding on my table. Let me close those wounds. I'll keep a little of what holds you together.
I've seen the road ahead, and frankly it was too comfortable. Let me move some furniture. You'll thank me. Eventually.

Sharper teeth, thinner skin. Surely a fair swap. Nobody has ever complained, at least not for long.
Holy water? Dull. I can do better, and I won't make you drink it. You look well. Rich, even. So let's talk about the one thing you haven't spent. Sign, and the road gets easy.

Eight gold for a damp blessing? Put the coin away. My gifts come with interest. Ahead there's a beast waiting for you. I can make it a hearth instead, for a modest donation of blood. Don't ask what's feeding the fire.
